> Collected traces from 08:20–09:00 and uploaded to s3 (same link in incident). Early look: there are repeated cases where the content-length in the header matches the original message, but an extra control byte (0x1f) is injected by a client middleware before the payload in ~0.4% of events. Our parser interprets that control byte as part of the header delimiter sequence in some codepaths, which causes the boundary index to move and drop the trailing chunk.
>
> I have a conservative mitigation ready: change the parser to treat any single unexpected control byte before payload as part of payload (i.e., shift boundary detection). That’s low-risk and can be rolled in canary within 2 hours, but it doesn’t address root cause — the client middleware is abusing the inline metadata header.

Confirmed — SDK instrumentation shows the client-side middleware (QuickRetail's auth proxy) is inserting an inline metadata control byte sequence for tracing. In the majority of integrations this is fine, but in a narrow window when the chunk header is exactly aligned with the injected data the parser state machine misclassifies the delimiter and yields a truncated payload.

Workarounds:
- ASK CUSTOMER: disable inline metadata injection in their proxy (fastest; requires one-line config change).
- SDK change: tolerate single leading control bytes (Marissa's mitigation) — deployable in 2 hours as emergency roll.
- Runtime policy: fall back to non-streaming for routes with detected mismatch for 24h while we push permanent fix.

I recommend applying the runtime fallback + Marissa's parser change simultaneously for safest outcome.

— Jonas
Principal SW Eng, Inference Runtime
